ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.561-2, L.561-2-2, L.561-4-1, L.561-5, L.561-6, L.561-10, L.561-10-2, L.561-15 and L.561-32; Code monétaire et financier, Articles R.561-1 to R.561-22; Code de commerce, Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 and R.561-55 to R.561-63; Ordinance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020; Decree No. 2020-118 of 12 February 2020; beneficial-owner information is filed with the register of beneficial owners maintained through the competent company-register filing system. The legal framework reflects EU Directive (EU) 2015/849, as amended, including Directive (EU) 2018/843, subject to the post-2022 CJEU judgment in Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 and subsequent French access restrictions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, depending on the issuing country and treaty status

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate power of attorney for incorporation, filing, and beneficial-owner declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authorized representative of the foreign corporate principal, with certification by a notary or equivalent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French sworn translator or translator authorized by a competent French court

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, onboarding, payment-account opening, and material ownership changes, screen all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and relevant counterparties against the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, European Union financial-sanctions lists, French national sanctions and asset-freeze measures, and OFAC SDN and applicable non-SDN lists. Apply a risk-based PEP and close-associate review under Code monétaire et financier Articles L.561-10 and R.561-18, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds review, senior-management approval, enhanced ongoing monitoring, adverse-media review, and documented false-positive resolution. OFAC screening is not generally mandatory for a purely French transaction but is required where a US nexus, US person, US dollar clearing, US technology, or contractual sanctions undertaking exists. Retain identification, screening, escalation, and decision records under applicable AML/CFT retention rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI): formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be stated in the incorporation documents and filing in a form accepted by the French register. French law does not generally require a company name to be written in French or in a particular local script. Latin characters are normally used in French filings; non-Latin names may require an acceptable transliteration or an accompanying Latin rendering for registry, tax, banking, and contractual purposes. The name must not create confusion with a protected prior company name, trade name, trademark, domain name, or geographical indication and must not be misleading, unlawful, or contrary to public order. Availability at the registry does not establish trademark clearance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words or expressions reserved to regulated professions, regulated financial activities, public authorities, public bodies, or protected legal forms without the required authorization

Banking, insurance, investment-services, payment, electronic-money, credit, finance, medical, pharmaceutical, legal, accounting, audit, and other regulated-sector terms where their use could imply an unlicensed activity
Terms suggesting a public authority, official status, national institution, intergovernmental organization, or public-service mandate
Protected designations and names covered by intellectual-property, geographical-indication, or sector-specific legislation
Deceptive, discriminatory, defamatory, unlawful, or public-order-incompatible expressions
Names confusingly similar to an existing registered company, trade name, trademark, or domain name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory company-name reservation period of 30 days for an SAS. A proposed name is checked during preparation and filing, but availability is not a definitive legal clearance and there is no universal reservation extension procedure. Conduct searches through the INPI company and trademark databases, Infogreffe or equivalent registry data, domain registries, and relevant sector registers. If the Guichet unique or registry rejects the name, obtain the rejection reason, correct the filing or propose an alternative name, and resubmit through the portal. For a formal administrative decision, request reconsideration from the issuing authority and, where legally available, file a recours gracieux or recours hiérarchique within two months of notification; a judicial challenge before the competent administrative or commercial court must be assessed according to the nature of the decision. Registry refusals affecting company-registration formalities may also be challenged through the competent court under the applicable Code de commerce procedure. A separate trademark objection or infringement issue must be handled before the competent industrial-property or judicial authority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An SAS must have a registered office in France under Code civil Article 1837 and Code de commerce Articles L.123-11 to L.123-11-5. A domiciliation company may provide a registered address only if it is authorized under the applicable commercial-domiciliation regime and the domiciliation agreement and premises satisfy statutory requirements. A director's home address may be used in limited circumstances subject to applicable confidentiality and procedural rules. A virtual office is generally acceptable for a lightweight consumer SaaS business with no regulated activity, inventory, staff, or customer-facing premises, provided that the company maintains reliable accounting, tax, banking, contractual, data-protection, and operational records and can receive official correspondence. A virtual address cannot substitute for genuine operational substance where tax residence, permanent-establishment, employment, transfer-pricing, consumer-protection, or payment-provider requirements require actual functions and personnel.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection for a low-risk, newly formed consumer micro-SaaS with no employees, regulated license, cash activity, or adverse AML indicators: approximately 0.5% to 2%. This is a risk estimate, not a statutory probability. The risk increases materially where there are inconsistent UBO records, a high-risk non-EU ownership chain, VAT anomalies, suspicious payment flows, sanctions or PEP alerts, consumer complaints, tax-residence concerns, suspected undeclared permanent establishment, or a domiciliation provider subject to supervisory review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, principally Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 to R.227-2 concerning the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 to L.123-9 concerning the Trade and Companies Register; applicable provisions of Articles L.123-36 and R.123-1 et seq. concerning the electronic One-Stop Business Formalities Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Registry of the Commercial Court (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce), with filings submitted electronically through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company formation filing (formalités de constitution) submitted through the Guichet Unique, supported by the signed SAS articles of association, beneficial ownership declaration, and required annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon subscription; the balance must be paid within five years of registration. Cash contributions are deposited with a qualifying bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, which issues the certificate of deposit. Contributions in kind must be fully contributed and may require a commissaire aux apports report, subject to statutory exemptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept the subscriptions for its issued shares and acknowledge payment of the required portion of each cash contribution, subject to the deposit certificate. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full French address], effective immediately. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed Président for an indefinite term, with authority to represent the Company within the limits of French law and the articles. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed Directeur Général, if applicable, with the powers specified in the articles and this resolution. The officers are authorized to complete all registration and banking formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Structure and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI; registered-office evidence supplied by the applicant.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the SAS name, corporate purpose, share capital, share classes, governance rules, Président, any Directeur Général, financial year, and French registered office. Obtain a domiciliation agreement, commercial lease, or proof of ownership. Ensure the address permits the proposed activity and retain evidence for filing.
required_dossiers: Identity and address evidence for officers
Power of attorney, if a representative files
Declaration of non-conviction and parentage for each individual officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace defective address evidence, correct the articles, or upload a signed clarification through the Guichet Unique response function before the registry deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Qualifying deposit-taking bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the final SAS articles and subscription forms. Open a temporary capital account, transfer at least 50% of cash subscriptions, and obtain the certificate of deposit. Document any contribution in kind and obtain a commissaire aux apports report unless a statutory exemption is validly applied.
required_dossiers: Source-of-funds information requested by the depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct subscriber identification, source-of-funds, or signature deficiencies and resubmit to the depositary. If the depositary refuses the account, obtain a written refusal and approach another qualifying institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company shareholders and appointed corporate officers; filing administered by INPI and reviewed by the competent commercial registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the shareholder decision approving the articles, appointing the Président and any Directeur Général, confirming the registered office, approving the capital subscription, and authorizing the incorporation filing. Execute the first board or management resolution where required by the articles. Obtain officer declarations of non-conviction and parentage.
required_dossiers: First management or board resolution, if applicable
Officer declarations of non-conviction and parentage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Adopt a corrective shareholder decision or resolution, replace missing signatures, and upload a consolidated corrected document set.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, with final registration by the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the SAS formation filing, complete the activity and establishment data, identify officers and beneficial owners, upload the required documents, pay the applicable registry and beneficial ownership fees, and electronically sign or validate the filing using the authorized filing method. Monitor the portal and registry messages until issuance of the SIREN, SIRET, and Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Translations by a sworn translator where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond electronically to any registry query within the stated deadline, correct the identified field or attachment, pay any additional fee, and resubmit. If rejected, request the rejection grounds and lodge the legally available registry or court remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique, commercial bank, tax administration, and relevant social-security bodies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Kbis extract and verify the SIREN, SIRET, legal name, activity, officers, and registered office. Release the deposited capital into the operating account, activate tax and social accounts, maintain statutory registers, and preserve the beneficial ownership record. Register for VAT where required by the business model and turnover rules.
required_dossiers: Payroll and social-registration documentation, if employees are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction from INPI or the registry for inaccurate registration data. File amended tax, social, or beneficial ownership information where subsequent changes occur.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for consumer micro-SaaS operated from ordinary office premises without manufacturing, industrial storage, regulated telecommunications infrastructure, or an independently operated data centre.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No dedicated manufacturing or industrial operating permit is ordinarily required for lightweight productivity cloud software operations. Ordinary commercial, employment, data-protection, consumer-law, and information-security obligations remain applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition; environmental review is administered through the competent regional environmental authority, typically the Mission Régionale d'Autorité environnementale (MRAe) and the relevant Préfet.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for ordinary SaaS office operations with no construction, industrial installation, or independently operated data centre. A project-specific environmental assessment may arise for construction or an installation classified under the ICPE regime.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No SaaS-specific wastewater or VOC thresholds apply where the company operates from ordinary offices and uses third-party cloud infrastructure. The company must comply with applicable waste-sorting, electrical-equipment, hazardous-substance, and workplace requirements. Any data centre, generator, cooling system, discharge, or industrial installation is assessed under applicable ICPE, water, air-emission, and waste rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial civil-defense clearance is ordinarily required for a standard SaaS office. The landlord or operator must address building safety, fire detection, evacuation routes, accessibility, and, where applicable, ERP obligations for premises open to the public. The employer must complete the occupational risk assessment in the DUERP, provide safe working conditions, and arrange legally required inspections. Structural-load, fire, and electrical certifications are required where imposed by the building, lease, works, or premises classification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French-resident entities obtain SIREN/SIRET automatically upon incorporation with commercial registry; foreign entities register through French tax representative or portal to acquire TVA identification number
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box elections; hybrid mismatch rules apply under ATAD framework; territorial taxation scope for French-source income

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing for B2B transactions since October 2024; real-time data exchange with tax authorities via APIs; digital VAT stamps required for compliant invoicing

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT on goods exported outside the EU; for digital services and SaaS, zero-rating applies if supplied to non-EU customers under place-of-supply rules (e.g., customer location-based for B2B)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims result in 80% penalty on evaded VAT plus interest; full clawback of zero-rated VAT with retroactive adjustments and potential criminal sanctions

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), a member of the Eurosystem, acting as the national central bank and the competent authority for balance-of-payments statistics and cross-border payment surveillance; foreign exchange policy and exchange-control direction are exercised by the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) within the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique; prudential and AML/CFT supervision of credit institutions and payment institutions is vested in the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution), with operational suspicious-transaction reporting to Tracfin.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full euro convertibility and unrestricted current-account and capital-account liberalization under Articles 63-66 TFEU and Articles L151-1 to L151-7 of the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF). There are no exchange-control barriers to profit remittance, dividend distribution, capital repatriation, or liquidation proceeds payable to non-resident shareholders of a French SAS. The only residual controls apply to foreign direct investment in national-security-sensitive sectors listed in Article R153-1 et seq. CMF, which does not cover ISIC 6201 software publishing. A French SAS distributing dividends to a non-resident corporate shareholder is normally subject to French withholding tax at 25% for non-treaty EEA shareholders, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the beneficial owner is an EU/EAA company holding at least 5% of the SAS capital for an uninterrupted two-year period; interest on shareholder loans is generally exempt. Cross-border transfers equal to or exceeding EUR 1,000 must be effected through a licensed credit institution and are reported for statistical purposes by the intermediary to the Banque de France; no prior administrative authorization is required for a consumer micro-SaaS treasury.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation deadline for export proceeds under current French law. A French SAS may lawfully retain export receipts in USD, GBP, or any other currency in resident or non-resident correspondent accounts with no obligation to convert into euros. The residual statutory obligation under Article L151-2 CMF is limited to routing cross-border transfers and payments through an approved credit institution or assimilated intermediary. Banque de France Instruction No. 91-01 imposes statistical declaration of each cross-border transaction equal to or exceeding EUR 1,000; for a micro-SaaS collecting export revenues via Paddle or Lemon Squeezy, the declaration is made by the payment institution or the acquiring bank, not by the exporting entity. Direct balance-of-payments filing by the SAS will arise only if the entity is selected in the Banque de France direct corporate survey, which depends on annual cross-border flow thresholds rather than FX holdings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Main operational euro corporate account (compte de dépôt) together with a segregated blocked capital escrow account (compte d'apport) for the constitutional deposit prior to SAS registration
Corporate transaction account for receivables and payables; dedicated capital escrow sub-account for the apport en numéraire

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: LCL / Crédit Lyonnais (Crédit Agricole S.A. group)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Professional operational account with e-banking treasury module and foreign-currency sub-account
Compte professionnel transactionnel with cross-border payment and short-term treasury services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. (Banque Populaire / Caisse d'Épargne corporate desks)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency operational account (compte en devises) for USD and GBP treasury settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for ACPR-licensed or EEA-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs) and digital banks, subject to significant legal constraints. An EMI such as Qonto, Shine, or Pennylane can lawfully hold client funds under the e-money Safeguarding rules, supports fully remote onboarding with video KYC, and provides API-driven multi-currency settlement rails suitable for the Paddle and Lemon Squeezy payout streams. However, an EMI is not a credit institution: client funds are safeguarded rather than deposited, are not covered by the French deposit guarantee fund (FGDR), and e-money issuance presumes an immediate exchange of funds into e-money, making the EMI unsuitable as the long-term home of share capital, VAT reserves, or payroll. An offshore non-EEA EMI without an ACPR passport or French branch registration cannot lawfully open a French-domiciled account or settle balances in the euro system; therefore, the treasury blueprint mandates a licensed Tier-1 bank account as the primary legal entity account and restricts fintech entities to the FX conversion and cross-border collection layer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required by Tier-1 French banks at least once for signature verification of the SAS president (président) or any appointed signatory, particularly where the ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident individual or a non-EEA holding entity. Modern regulated banks accept eIDAS-compliant video-identity verification and remote electronic signature for low-risk software corporations, but the compliance teams of BNP Paribas and Société Générale retain discretion to request a physical branch interview before activation of cross-border payments. The recommended treasury strategy is to combine the initial corporate incorporation trip to Paris with a single bank onboarding meeting, complete the original signature-card formalities, and thereafter migrate all treasury administration, SWIFT access, and FX instructions to secure remote channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO chain holding the French SAS through a low-tax or secrecy-jurisdiction intermediary, causing the bank's AML engine to flag the entity as a transshipment vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current extract from the French Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) produced within statutory filing times; complete ownership chart from the ultimate individual shareholder down to the SAS; apostilled constitutional documents and share registers for each intermediate holding company; valid tax residence certificates; sworn explanatory memorandum demonstrating economic substance, actual SaaS activity, operational headcount in France, and the absence of any tax-evasion or concealment purpose; plus annual financial projections demonstrating commercial rationale for the French SAS.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue concentration in e-commerce aggregator merchant-of-record models (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) presenting bulk, commingled settlement files that obscure the underlying B2C or micro-B2B licences
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-cycle merchant settlement and payout reconciliation reports from the payment processors; breakdown of gross vs net settlement and all platform fees; the processor's own AML/KYB status and regulatory licence; French VAT registration and EU OSS confirmation to prove tax compliance; monthly certified sales journal and customer invoicing file; and the SAS's standard terms of sale demonstrating licensing, refund, and chargeback procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the registered office (domiciliation address) declared at the Companies Registry and the operational treasury address from which FX and bank instructions are actually executed
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-agent domiciliation certificate covering the statutory registered office; commercial lease or ownership deed for the operational premises; Kbis extract showing the registered address; internal organizational chart and treasury policy designating the persons empowered to issue SWIFT/e-banking instructions; bank mandate form listing the operational signatory categories; and a written explanation of remote-work treasury management consistent with the bank's wire-transfer verification procedures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For initial formation, the non-resident shareholder wires the appel de fonds in euros via SWIFT MT103 to a blocked deposit account (compte bloqué) held either at the chosen French Tier-1 bank or at the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the wire must identify the payer as the exact named shareholder, reference the SAS corporate name and intended SIREN, and carry in Field 70 the indication 'APPORT EN NUMÉRAIRE / CONSTITUTION DE SAS' to allow the bank to issue the statutory deposit certificate (certificat du dépositaire des fonds). After the SAS obtains its Kbis registration, the blocked funds are released to the operational account. For a subsequent capital increase, the same MT103 protocol applies with reference to the notarial or board resolution increasing capital and the corresponding registry filing. French exchange-control neutrality means no prior authorization is required, but the intermediary bank will include the inbound flow in its Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting and the company must preserve the full upstream source-of-funds documentation, including bank statements of the sending account and the shareholders' agreement, to satisfy ongoing AML reviews.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All EU-based disbursements for cloud infrastructure, subcontractors, and statutory expenses settle through the SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) scheme using the operational account IBAN, with SEPA Instant available for urgent sub-EUR 100,000 payments. Payments outside the eurozone, including US-based cloud providers and any non-EU suppliers, settle via SWIFT MT103 through the French bank's correspondent network, with strict consistency between the invoice amount, the SWIFT amount, and the payment reference to avoid transfer-pricing or trade-data mismarches; documentary trade instruments are not necessary for SaaS licensing flows. A commercial letter of credit is structurally permissible but economically inappropriate for recurring software subscriptions and is reserved only for exceptional high-value procurement of physical hardware where the beneficiary requires a bank-backed undertaking. For treasury optimisation, the USD and GBP balances created by Paddle and Lemon Squeezy settlements may be held on multi-currency accounts and converted through the bank's spot desk rather than undergoing wasteful double conversion through the EMI layer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX outright transactions (EUR/USD and EUR/GBP) executed through the Tier-1 bank treasury desk or regulated digital-brokerage channels for immediate conversion of PSP settlement balances

Plain-vanilla FX forward contracts (outright forwards) up to 12 months, documented under the FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) Master Agreement or ISDA, available for hedging anticipated monthly USD and GBP receipts from Paddle and Lemon Squeezy, provided the notional does not exceed forecast commercial exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), permissible only where the deliverable EUR/USD or EUR/GBP forward market is unavailable or illiquid; not expected to be used for this micro-SaaS treasury
FX swaps (swap de change) for short-term liquidity smoothing where USD settlement float is swapped into euro funding for VAT or payroll cycles

Cross-currency swaps (xCCY), admissible for medium-term intercompany shareholder loans and capital injections, subject to MiFID II appropriateness, derivative-clearing eligibility review, and the prohibition of speculative uncovered positions

European-style currency options (call and put structures) permitted for the SAS as an end-user hedging instrument against adverse USD/EUR or GBP/EUR movements, purchased only as protection on identified licensing receivables or supplier payables and never in a naked speculative capacity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory financial statements (bilan, compte de résultat, annexe) filed with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of fiscal year-end; if shareholders approve earlier, within 1 month after approval. For calendar-year SAS, filing must occur by 30 June (7 months after 31 December).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an administrative fine under Article L.232-23 and R.232-12 of the French Commercial Code (up to EUR 5,000 for a legal entity), possible compelled deposition, and repeated default may lead to RCS strike-off (radiation).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats n° 2065 and liasse fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service des Impôts des Entreprises (French Business Tax Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year ending 31 December, file by the second business day after 1 May (electronic filing mandatory). For non-calendar year-ends, file within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late filing triggers a 10% automatic late-payment penalty (CGI art. 1728), plus delay interest of 0.2% per month; repeated default can lead to revised assessment, legal prosecution, and additional civil sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register update / declaration (where ownership changed; no annual filing required if unchanged)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS), via the 'registre des bénéficiaires effectifs' mechanism
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days; the annual general meeting minutes should also confirm the continuing accuracy of the UBO register as an internal annual control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is criminally punishable under C. mon. fin. art. L.561-47 and R.561-30, exposing natural persons to up to EUR 10,000 fine and 2 years' imprisonment; legal entities face separate criminal sanctions and possible registry action leading to strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting resolution approving annual accounts (procès-verbal d'assemblée générale ordinaire)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records – minute book held at the registered office; no separate regulatory filing for this document
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be adopted within 6 months after the close of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The SAS president may face civil liability for failure to convene the meeting; shareholders or the public prosecutor may request court-ordered convening, and repeated non-approval of accounts may constitute ground for judicial dissolution or extra-contractual damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CFE (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises) – annual declaration and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – local business tax service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment due by 15 December each year; electronic payment available until 20 December for companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid CFE accrues interest at 0.2% per month plus a 10% uplift; the tax authority may issue an enforcement writ and commence asset recovery proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) for an SAS only if at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded at the year-end: total balance sheet > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (excl. VAT) > EUR 8,000,000; average workforce > 50 employees. A micro-SaaS entity under these thresholds is exempt unless it controls or is controlled by another French entity meeting the thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général / ANC regulations and Code de commerce) governs individual statutory accounts. IFRS is permitted only for consolidated group accounts on a voluntary basis, not for the SAS's annual statutory return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing. The SAS is required to keep the 'registre des bénéficiaires effectifs' at its registered office and to file any change with the trade registry within 30 days. As an annual corporate governance measure, the ordinary shareholders' meeting (or a designated register audit) should reaffirm the register's accuracy in writing, recording such verification in the minute book.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Securities Ledger (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Directors and Corporate Officers (registre des présidents/DGs and decision records)
Minute Book (registre des décisions sociales / procès-verbaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250 – $650 per year (EUR 230 – EUR 600), depending on domiciliation service provider in Paris or regional cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000 – $9,000 (EUR 3,700 – EUR 8,500) only if an auditor is appointed voluntarily; statutory audit is normally not required for a micro-SaaS entity below the legal thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax rate. A 3.3% social contribution may apply to companies meeting the statutory turnover and corporate income tax liability thresholds, producing a potential marginal combined rate of approximately 25.83%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may benefit from a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory conditions, including turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% ownership by individuals or qualifying entities. Eligible research and development expenditure may qualify for the French research tax credit, generally 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold. The credit is not an automatic industry incentive and requires substantiation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward under French law; the prescribed five-year limitation does not apply. Annual utilization is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally limited to the preceding financial year and subject to statutory amount limits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French tax administration portal impots.gouv.fr using the professional account, generally through EDI-TDFC or EFI. Supporting tax packages normally include forms 2058-A, 2058-B, 2058-C, 2059-A to 2059-G and applicable sector-specific schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate income tax installments are generally payable quarterly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the annual return and tax balance are generally due by the second business day after 1 May of the following year, commonly 15 May. For other year-ends, the return is generally due within three months after year-end. Corporate income tax installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions and adjustment rules. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, fiscal year opening and closing dates, principal activity, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent does not replace the French SAS as the filing entity. Report the French company's own SIREN, French registered office and French accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result determined from French statutory accounts after tax adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, depreciation restrictions and other reconciliation items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income and expenses attributable to the French SAS. Payments to foreign related parties must be supported by transfer pricing evidence and withholding tax analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit, applicable rate, gross corporate income tax, credits, instalments, withholding credits and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the ordinary 25% rate unless a valid statutory reduced-rate regime applies. Treaty relief generally does not reduce the French SAS's own corporate income tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation between accounting profit or loss and taxable profit or loss, including permanent and temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign accounting entries must be translated and reconciled into the French tax computation. Foreign taxes and foreign exchange items require separate deductibility and credit analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax losses, carried-forward losses used, remaining losses and any carried-back loss claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French unlimited carryforward regime and the annual utilization cap. Do not apply a generic five-year expiration rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and reductions, including eligible research tax credit claims where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claims must be supported by French statutory eligibility records, project documentation, personnel costs, subcontractor evidence and expenditure allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Short-term and long-term capital gains or losses and applicable tax treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder's disposal of SAS shares is generally analyzed separately under French domestic law and the applicable treaty; it is not automatically included in the SAS's operating result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2059-C to 2059-G, participation and related tax information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning exempt participation gains, provisions, shareholdings and other required corporate tax disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose relevant French and foreign related-party interests and transactions consistently with statutory accounts, related-party registers and transfer pricing records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of specified extraordinary or non-routine expenses, including certain remuneration, benefits and exceptional payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-parent charges, management fees, exceptional bonuses and shareholder-related expenses require clear business purpose and arm's-length support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly installments, credits and final balance payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent should fund the French SAS sufficiently to meet payment dates; failure caused by shareholder cash-flow arrangements remains the SAS's liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic transmission of the return and electronic settlement through the professional tax account or authorized EDI provider.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain an authorized French filing representative, accounting provider or internal user with valid professional-account credentials. Paper filing is generally not an acceptable substitute for mandatory electronic filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed returns may attract a 10% surcharge, increased in aggravated cases, plus late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month. Failure to file electronically may trigger an additional 0.20% charge, generally subject to a minimum amount. Underpayment may also generate surcharges, interest, audit adjustments and penalties for intentional, abusive or fraudulent conduct. Late payment of installments can create collection interest and enforcement costs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Forms 2777-SD and applicable withholding-tax declarations, filed electronically through the professional tax account where required, for distributions and certain payments subject to French withholding tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Event-driven or monthly, generally by the 15th day of the month following payment or distribution, subject to the specific payment category.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Withholding tax is generally declared and paid by the 15th day of the month following the payment, booking or making-available event, depending on the relevant statutory rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recipient identity, address, tax residence and payment category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain and retain the foreign recipient's tax residence certificate, beneficial ownership statement and treaty-relief documentation before applying a reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross dividend, interest, royalty or other relevant payment before withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the legally relevant gross amount and do not net the payment against foreign taxes, bank fees or intercompany balances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable French domestic withholding rate, reduced treaty rate or exemption code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty relief only where the treaty, beneficial ownership, anti-abuse and documentation conditions are satisfied. Otherwise withhold at the domestic rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding amount, payment date, tax office and remittance details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS remains liable as withholding agent even where the foreign beneficiary contractually bears the tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or inaccurate withholding declarations may result in tax recovery, a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest, penalties for failure to withhold, and additional sanctions where the omission is deliberate or fraudulent.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The standard French withholding tax on dividends distributed by a French company to a non-resident recipient is generally 25%, subject to applicable exemptions and tax treaties. A qualifying EU or European Economic Area parent may obtain an exemption under the French implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, commonly requiring at least 10% ownership for the relevant holding period and satisfaction of anti-abuse and beneficial-owner conditions. A 75% rate may apply to certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions or territories.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a current certificate of tax residence from the recipient's tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, minimum holding and anti-abuse conditions, and retain the ownership chain and commercial-purpose evidence. Apply the reduced rate at source only where French administrative conditions permit. Otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and pursue a refund claim through the French tax administration using the applicable treaty claim forms and supporting certificate. Treaty relief is treaty-specific; France does not have one uniform dividend, interest or royalty rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to a domestic withholding rate of 25%, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and potentially a 75% rate for certain non-cooperative jurisdictions. Ordinary interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to standard French withholding tax, although exceptions apply, including certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, anti-abuse cases and specific instruments or arrangements. Treaty rates vary by recipient country and payment classification. EU interest and royalty relief may be available where the statutory associated-company, holding-period, beneficial-ownership and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory full transfer pricing documentation generally applies where the French entity or French tax group has annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, where it is controlled by or controls an entity meeting the threshold, or where it belongs to a group meeting the applicable statutory conditions. Large groups may also have country-by-country reporting obligations, generally where consolidated group revenue reaches EUR 750 million. Below the threshold, French taxpayers must still demonstrate arm's-length pricing and provide simplified or appropriate documentation on request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no separate UAE-style economic substance regulation applicable solely because a company receives foreign income. Substance is assessed through general anti-abuse rules, transfer pricing, permanent establishment, beneficial ownership, controlled foreign company, interest limitation, withholding tax and abuse-of-law doctrines. A French SAS should maintain genuine French decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or documented operating arrangements, accounting records, bank control, customer and supplier evidence, and commercial rationale proportionate to its SaaS activity. Artificial conduit arrangements, circular cash flows and shareholder-controlled expenses may be recharacterized or denied.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.micro_saas_specific_controls: Document the ownership and licensing of software code, trademarks, domains, datasets and customer contracts; allocate development, hosting, support, marketing and platform fees using functional analysis; benchmark recurring cross-border service, royalty and cost-sharing charges; reconcile Paddle and Lemon Squeezy settlement reports to French revenue, refunds, chargebacks, VAT and payment fees; and maintain evidence for the place of supply and customer location of digital services.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing taxable SaaS revenue, fabricating expenses, omitting payment-platform receipts, knowingly filing false accounts, or using sham invoices to reduce corporate income tax or VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, tax fraud penalties, interest and criminal prosecution. Ordinary tax fraud may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated cases potentially carrying up to seven years' imprisonment and a fine of up to EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions and judicial determination.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, imprisonment, asset seizure and director disqualification. Courts may impose personal tax liability on a manager under Article L.267 of the French Tax Procedures Code where fraudulent or repeated serious failures made collection from the company impossible. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be ordered in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying electronically supplied services, failing to charge or remit French or EU VAT, manipulating customer location evidence, or excluding Paddle or Lemon Squeezy receipts from books.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessment, late-payment interest, 10% or higher surcharges, possible 40% or 80% tax penalties depending on conduct, payment-platform information matching, and criminal prosecution for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for deliberate or repeated VAT fraud, tax collection failure, criminal fines, seizure and disqualification. Personal liability requires the applicable statutory or judicial basis and is not automatic merely because a company has unpaid VAT.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, development charges or cost allocations to shift SaaS profit abroad, or maintaining no functional analysis or supporting comparables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment to French taxable income, withholding tax reassessment, interest, documentation penalties, and possible application of the French anti-abuse or abnormal-management-act doctrines. The tax administration may reject unsupported deductions and recharacterize transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where they knowingly orchestrate fraudulent profit shifting, conceal records or facilitate tax fraud. Routine transfer pricing adjustment alone does not automatically create criminal or personal director liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS solely as a conduit, maintaining no real business activity, routing customer receipts through undisclosed foreign entities, backdating contracts, or paying profits to an entity lacking personnel, functions and decision-making.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of income, permanent establishment exposure, withholding tax, corporate tax reassessment, abuse-of-law penalties and potential criminal sanctions where concealment or fraud is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may face civil claims, criminal prosecution, asset seizure and disqualification if they knowingly operate an artificial structure for unlawful tax avoidance or concealment. A lack of substance is not by itself a criminal offence but is a major evidentiary risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing cash without distributable profits or reserves, making shareholder advances, booking personal expenses as business costs, or disguising dividends as royalties, salaries, loans or consulting fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, corporate tax reassessment, withholding tax, denied deductions, penalties and potential breach of French corporate law rules governing distributions and related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may owe civil restitution, damages and potentially criminal penalties for unlawful distributions or misuse of corporate assets. Shareholders who knowingly receive unlawful distributions may also be required to repay them.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained funds, concealing beneficial ownership, using nominee shareholders, structuring payments to evade controls, or failing to identify counterparties and beneficial owners where AML obligations apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious transaction reporting obligations, account restrictions, confiscation, administrative sanctions and criminal money-laundering penalties. Aggravated money laundering may carry substantial imprisonment and fines, subject to the applicable facts and statutory provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who participate in or knowingly facilitate laundering may face imprisonment, personal fines, confiscation and disqualification. Directors may also face regulatory sanctions for serious governance or compliance failures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Bribery, corruption and improper commercial payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Offering or accepting payments, benefits, commissions or concealed rebates to obtain customers, public contracts, licenses, tax treatment or platform access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution, imprisonment and substantial fines for active or passive corruption, confiscation of proceeds, procurement exclusion and corporate liability. Exact sanctions depend on the offence and circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals may be prosecuted personally regardless of corporate form. Directors may face imprisonment, fines, confiscation, disqualification and civil claims; the SAS may incur separate corporate criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Destroying invoices, source code ownership records, payment-platform statements, customer-location evidence or accounting data; refusing access during an audit; or maintaining materially false books.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties, rejection of accounting records, estimated assessment, criminal accounting or tax-fraud proceedings, and increased penalties for obstruction or deliberate concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal fines, imprisonment, civil damages and disqualification where they ordered, approved or knowingly tolerated destruction or falsification of records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Foreign exchange, sanctions and restricted-party breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing SaaS services, software, encryption or payments to sanctioned persons, embargoed territories or restricted industries without required screening, authorization or controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Payment blocking, asset freezing, administrative and criminal penalties, confiscation, contractual termination and regulatory enforcement under applicable French and EU sanctions rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal criminal exposure where they knowingly authorize or negligently facilitate prohibited transactions. Corporate veil protection does not shield intentional sanctions violations.
